selection_manifest.human_review_reason: This source presents a compound of significant credibility concerns that collectively justify a low credibility rating, despite the high authority of the underlying organization (OCHA). The canonical URL resolves to an X.com (Twitter) post from the @OCHA_Ethiopia account — a social media post, not a formal report or structured data publication. Several critical misalignments are present: (1) Geographic mismatch: The account handle is OCHA_Ethiopia, but the collection task targets Haiti. The query that surfaced this result was Haiti-specific, suggesting this is a false positive from the search discovery process rather than a genuinely relevant source. (2) Disease relevance is ambiguous: No target disease terms (cholera) were found in the source metadata. The disease_relevance_score of 0.20 is very low, and the source_disease_relevance_status is flagged as 'ambiguous_disease'. (3) Platform risk: X.com posts are ephemeral, unstructured, and not citable as primary data sources. Even if the post references a formal OCHA situation report, the post itself cannot serve as a data source — only the underlying report it links to (if any) would be eligible. (4) Publisher is null, and the source_type label of 'international_organization_report' is misleading — this is a social media post, not a report. The label inflation increases the risk of downstream misclassification. (5) The deterministic assessor flagged 'screening_and_critic_disagree', indicating internal inconsistency in the pipeline's evaluation of this source. (6) The title snippet ('Situation Report In 2024, humanitarian partners & the Govt. of ...') is truncated and does not confirm Haiti or cholera relevance. The high authority_score (0.88) reflects OCHA's institutional standing, but authority alone does not confer data usability when the platform, geography, and disease relevance are all misaligned.
